title: Recording: Name And Address, Girls School, London Town, Girlfriend by Wings | 1977
content:
Studio Three, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Peter Henderson, Mark Vigars

Wings began recording their sixth studio album London Town on 14 February 1977.

The first song recorded was ‘Name And Address’. The basic track had Paul McCartney on bass guitar and guide vocals, Linda McCartney on electric piano, Jimmy McCulloch and Denny Laine on electric guitars, and Joe English on drums.

Two tape reels were filled before the band moved on. The next song was ‘Girls School’, which was released on a double a-side single with ‘Mull Of Kintyre’. This time Paul switched to piano, and Linda played Moog synthesizer.

The third song was ‘London Town’. The backing track had Paul on piano, Laine on acoustic guitar, McCulloch on electric guitar, and English on drums.

The final song of the day was ‘Girlfriend’, which had been written in 1973. Paul switched back to bass guitar, but the line-up was otherwise the same as on ‘London Town’.
